Headline: Jan. 1969
Text: John Roberts, Joel Rosenman, Artie Kornfeld and Michael Lang form Woodstock Ventures Inc. to use festivals as an investment opportunity (History.com.)

Headline: Aug. 12, 1994
Text: Wanting to celebrate 25 years since the successful original Woodstock festival, Lang threw together Woodstock '94. According to The Daily Campus, it was a "prelude" to the mess of Woodstock '99 as music trends had changed tremendously and there was a lot of rain.

Headline: July 1997
Text: Woodstock '99 is announced. This time, it would be organized by just Lang and John Scher, the head of Metropolitan Entertainment.

Headline: July 22, 1999
Text: Woodstock '99 begins with a performance from James Brown (EBSCO.)

Headline: July 24, 1999
Text: Nu-metal band Limp Bizkit delivers an infamous performance of "Break Stuff" at the festival, often still blamed today for instigating the riots at the festival.

Headline: July 25, 1999
Text: The Red Hot Chili Peppers close out the festival. Unfortunately, the riots and chaos only escalated.
